The fsm change adds commands/fsm.md to the test -f list at :20 and adds three content greps for skills/fsm/SKILL.md at :125-127, but adds none for commands/fsm.md. commands/fsm.md carries the exit-code table users act on (0/3/2/1, the resume_hint fork note, 'A mock: true run never satisfies a gate'), and that prose could be emptied or contradicted without any test failing. findings.note: The change pins the FSM test fixture but not the FSM test that reads it, and the suite runner treats that test as optional. tests/manifest/test-skills.sh:20 now asserts tests/go/agent-prompt-anchors.txt and testdata/fsm/agent-prompt.golden exist, but tests/go/test-fsm.sh — the only consumer of both (test-fsm.sh:66) and the entire 239-line FSM suite added by this branch — is not pinned anywhere, and tests/run-all.sh:46 invokes it as 'if [ -f tests/go/test-fsm.sh ]; then ...'. Deleting or renaming that file therefore removes all FSM coverage while run-all.sh exits 0 and this manifest test still passes on the orphaned fixtures. The if-guard is a pre-existing pattern applied to all 30-odd suites in run-all.sh and is not introduced by this shard, so this is advisory rather than blocking; but this shard is where the FSM manifest contract is being written, and pinning the fixture without its consumer is the asymmetry that makes the hole reachable. Adding tests/go/test-fsm.sh to the :20 list closes it for the new suite at no cost.
